reviews.review: I like the lemurians! What interesting little specimens.
I have no idea what it is about this game.. It just hits right.. like everytime.

Boring roguelike, Feels good to complete once and forget about it.

Gameplay loop in runs is very repetitive. Characters have greats kits and a lot of synergy between skills. But as run goes on combat quickly degrades, often it is best to just hold jump button and spam all skills into horde or boss behind you.
Game's only main dodging mechanic is short jump, enemies themselves are boring and have little variety, enemy attacks constantly overlap so entire gameplan is holding jump with no strategy. There are always large horde of enemies and the best way to deal with them is constantly walking away and throwing few skills at them, there are no target priority or interesting positioning in 2D game, character traits die out and there is no room to use their skills more effectively than just "shoot at the biggest horde".
There is no macro play in this game, just pick up and buy everything you see. There is barely any time management, finding teleporter and interest spots is purely random process, routing is extremely basic and there is always clear shortest path from point A to B. Stage clearing is very boring and there is barely any strategy involved.

Runs are very repetitive, so if you are looking for Roguelike to play for a while then Risk of Rain Returns is horrible pick. But game still has a lot of content to experience for the first time, providence trials are nice set of minigames and each character is still decently unique, artstyle is pretty, game wont leave a bad taste after getting all unlocks n stuff.

Guys, I love this game!!

The original Risk of Rain (2013) was my entry into rougelike games as a genre and became one of my favorite games of all time. This remake does it incredible justice. 

The roster of items, enemies, characters, and abilities has been massively increased, and each has had so much time, thought, and care put into them that the overall quality is apparent from your first moments in the game, and continues to be hundreds of hours later. 

I also have to mention that the art and animations are stunning. The environments each have such a unique atmosphere and are beautifully rendered, with many details and secrets to find. Even unlocking new entries in the logbook is such a treat just for the art of the monsters and survivors alone.

My only real gripe with the game is that the description of some item and ability effects are pretty vague, even in the logbook. Also the internet says alot of them have numbers that are flat out wrong, lol. But to me, this isn't a very big deal.

The love the devs poured into this game is overwhelming and I think they did a fantastic job. If you like rougelike games with high difficulty*, depth, and variety, I recommend trying this game. 

(*they also added some really neat accessibility features that allow you to fine tune the difficulty to your exact preference if you think it's too hard or too easy, so don't be too put off by this if it isn't your cup of tea, I personally really enjoy a difficult challenge, and RoRR definitely delivers!)
